subject: N5-Level Performance Engineering for AI Workloads: Optimizing for Speed
body:
Hello First Name,

Our latest 🦄 ai that works session focused on N5-Level Performance Engineering for AI Workloads: Optimizing for Speed.

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot in the session. Here's a quick recap of the key points:

*   **The Performance Engineering Loop**: We explored the core loop and how AI agents are changing the approach. The bottleneck is shifting from brainstorming ideas to the crucial 'measurement' phase, which means less time spent guessing and more time validating.
*   **Fundamental Principles for Speed**: We discussed two core ideas: 'do less work' (think optimizing instructions, memory, and caches) and 'do more work at the same time' (through parallelism).
*   **Advanced Agentic Workflows**: We dove into nanosecond-level optimization using agentic workflows. This included strategies like aggressive code deletion, careful context management (using annotations and frequent restatements), and embracing the inherently experimental nature of performance engineering.

If you have any questions, just reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We're always happy to help! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
call_to_action: Check out the session recording and code on GitHub, and join our Discord for questions!
